To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diurnal course of nutrient concentrations in xylem sap of Ricinus communus plants is determined by plant-internal regulation and not by external conditions.

(1) the concentrations of ions in the xylemsap are highly correlated with each other, (2) the concentrations of nitrate are not coupled to the concentrations of other ions in the xylesap, (3) nitratetransport in the xylemmay not be coupled to the transport of other ions, and (4) the transport of nitrate to the shoot may be delayed with respect to its uptake by the roots.

(1) the diurnal variation in concentrations and flux in the root-to-shoot pathway of Ricinus is largely independent of nutrient supply, (2) nitrate flux to and uptake by the shoot are largely decoupled, and (3) the concomitantly increased nitrate concentrations and fluxes are delayed and transient.

the diurnal course of concentrations of nutrients in xylem sap is a result of a combination of plant-internal and environmental factors.
diurnal variations in xylem sap concentration and nutrient flux are not a consequence of changes in nutrient availability in the soil.

the dynamics of nutrient transport in xylem are largely determined by the plant’s own internal processes, which can be studied under controlled conditions.
